answer: Operator lien transfers. Each identity's rewards flow into a shared vault tied to its operator's payout history, so clones cannot withdraw independently. A rising tide of one operator's flags raises the release delay across all their identities at once. A prism check splits any payout across the operator's full identity count, so cloning dilutes rather than multiplies returns. Each added identity costs the attacker a full fraud-deposit and permanently slows every payout they control.
